answer: Latency-anchored identity relay. Each new identity must relay real traffic through an existing bridge node for one epoch before gaining write access. The bridge samples round-trip timing and cross-checks against a jetty of independent witnesses; clones sharing infrastructure show correlated jitter and get throttled below the zenith of usable throughput. An attacker pays real compute and bandwidth per clone while each adds near-zero reachable capacity, so marginal clones run at a loss.
